newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan gives tribal areas full voting rights.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan gives tribal areas full voting rights.

text.p: President Farooq Leghari said on Thursday that the caretaker government had granted people living in Pakistan's semi-autonomous tribal areas full voting rights in national elections for the first time.

"We have done something which is very revolutionary and which has extended democracy in Pakistan's last remaining bastion which was outside the adult franchise system -- the tribal area of Pakistan," he told Reuters in an interview.
He said the caretaker cabinet had approved a law earlier on Thursday to extend full voting rights to an estimated two million people living in the tribal areas.
The wild, mountainous marches on the Afghan border have traditionally been controlled by well-armed tribesmen and have provided havens for drug smugglers, kidnappers and bandits.

Under a system inherited from British colonial rule, the government's writ does not run beyond the few main roads in the tribal areas, including the road that winds through the rugged Khyber Pass into neighbouring Afghanistan.
The British-drawn frontier exists only on paper for many of the tribes, who have branches in both countries.
In the past the tribal areas have elected eight members of the National Assembly (lower house), who in turn elected eight members of the Senate (upper house).
The National Assembly members were elected by electoral colleges with memberships ranging from 1,600 to 3,200 voters.

"Now the electoral college will consist of every adult citizen of Pakistan living in those areas above the age of 21 years," Leghari said. "Almost all political parties had been promising this over the last 40 to 50 years. We have done that."

Leghari, who dissolved the National Assembly on November 5 and sacked Benazir Bhutto's government on disputed charges of corruption and misrule, said the caretaker government he had installed would hold fresh elections as scheduled on February 3.
He said preparation of electoral rolls, which normally takes up to six weeks, would be speeded up to allow polls to be held in the tribal areas on the same day as elsewhere in Pakistan.
"Nominations, too, will be on the date stipulated for the rest of the country." he said. "So that is a big move forward."
